provisions.title: Cap on security deposit and its refund
provisions.summary: Security deposit cannot be more than 2 months' rent for a home (6 months for non-residential premises). The landlord must refund it when he takes back vacant possession, after deducting only what the tenant actually owes.
provisions.caveat: This is a model law. It binds only in states that have passed their own tenancy law based on it. Many states still follow older rent control laws, so always ask which state the property is in.
provisions.keywords: security deposit advance refund landlord tenant rent kiraya jama makaan malik kirayedar flat room pg vacate shifting deduction

provisions.title: Compensation for breach of contract
provisions.summary: When one side breaks a contract (for example, a rent agreement or a job offer), the other side can claim compensation for the loss that naturally arises from that breach. Remote or indirect losses are not covered.
provisions.caveat: You must show the contract (written or proved by conduct) and the actual loss.
provisions.keywords: contract agreement breach compensation damages rent agreement promise loss deposit refund

provisions.title: Time limit for money recovery suits
provisions.summary: Where no other article of the Schedule applies, a civil suit must be filed within 3 years from the day the right to sue arises. Most suits to recover money, such as a withheld deposit, must be filed within about 3 years.
provisions.caveat: Courts sometimes apply a different article to deposits, and the start date can differ. If you are close to 3 years, see a lawyer quickly.
provisions.keywords: time limit limitation deadline how long late old years civil suit recovery money

provisions.title: Summary suit for a fixed sum under a written contract
provisions.summary: A faster civil suit is available for recovering a fixed amount of money that is due under a written contract. The other side can defend only if the court gives them permission ('leave to defend').
provisions.caveat: Needs a written contract and only works in notified courts. Usually filed through a lawyer.
provisions.keywords: civil suit court recovery summary suit written agreement fixed amount sue landlord employer

provisions.title: Two months' notice before suing the Government
provisions.summary: Before filing a civil suit against the Government or a public officer for an official act, you must send a written notice and wait two months.
provisions.caveat: Applies only when the other side is the Government or a public officer acting officially.
provisions.keywords: government department public officer municipal corporation notice before suit sarkari

provisions.title: Who gets a free government lawyer
provisions.summary: Free legal aid is available to: women and children, members of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, persons with disabilities, industrial workmen, victims of trafficking or disasters, people in custody, and anyone whose income is below the limit set by the government. Apply at the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) or call 15100.
provisions.caveat: Income limits differ between states and courts.
provisions.keywords: free lawyer legal aid cannot afford poor nalsa dlsa 15100 vakil free help mufat

provisions.title: Lok Adalat settlement is final
provisions.summary: A settlement reached in a Lok Adalat is treated like a civil court decree. It is final and binding on both sides, and there is no appeal against it.
provisions.caveat: Lok Adalat works only if both sides agree to settle.
provisions.keywords: lok adalat settlement compromise mediation quick cheap

provisions.act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
provisions.title: New criminal laws replaced IPC and CrPC
provisions.summary: From 1 July 2024, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC). Section numbers changed. The old codes still apply to offences committed before that date.
provisions.caveat: Haqdaar does not advise on criminal matters. A notice that threatens a criminal case needs a lawyer.
provisions.keywords: ipc crpc bns bnss criminal case fir police threat cheating fraud 420

provisions.title: Who is a consumer
provisions.summary: You are a consumer if you bought goods or paid for a service for your own use, including online. Someone who buys to resell or for a commercial purpose is usually not a consumer, unless it is for earning a livelihood through self-employment.
provisions.caveat: Business-to-business purchases are usually outside consumer law.
provisions.keywords: consumer buyer customer online shopping purchase grahak

provisions.title: Deficiency in service
provisions.summary: A 'deficiency' is any fault, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality or manner of a service that the seller or provider promised or is required to give. Not giving a promised refund or service can be a deficiency.
provisions.keywords: deficiency service bad service not delivered cancelled flight course gym refund not given

provisions.title: Unfair trade practice, including not refunding
provisions.summary: Unfair trade practices include misleading claims, and also refusing to take back defective goods or withdraw a deficient service and refund the money within the period stated on the bill, or within 30 days if no period is stated.
provisions.keywords: refund not given 30 days return defective product unfair trade practice misleading advertisement fake offer paisa wapas

provisions.act: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, with the Jurisdiction Rules, 2021
provisions.title: District Consumer Commission and where to file
provisions.summary: The District Consumer Commission hears complaints where the price paid for the goods or service is up to Rs 50 lakh. You can file where the seller is, where the problem arose, or where you live or work.
provisions.caveat: Above Rs 50 lakh the State Commission hears the case, and above Rs 2 crore the National Commission.
provisions.keywords: consumer court forum district commission where to file jurisdiction amount

provisions.title: Filing a consumer complaint, including online
provisions.summary: A consumer can file a complaint personally, without a lawyer, and it can be filed electronically. Online filing is done on the e-Jagriti portal (e-jagriti.gov.in), which replaced e-Daakhil on 1 January 2025.
provisions.keywords: how to file consumer complaint online e-jagriti edaakhil portal without lawyer

provisions.title: Two-year time limit for consumer complaints
provisions.summary: A consumer complaint must be filed within 2 years from the date the problem (cause of action) arose. The Commission can accept a late complaint if you show sufficient reason for the delay.
provisions.keywords: time limit consumer complaint how late deadline two years

provisions.act: Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020
provisions.title: No fee for small consumer claims
provisions.summary: There is no filing fee at the District Commission when the value of the goods or service paid for is up to Rs 5 lakh. Above that, the fee rises in steps.
provisions.keywords: fee cost filing fee free consumer complaint how much

provisions.title: E-commerce grievance officer deadlines
provisions.summary: Every e-commerce company must have a grievance officer, who must acknowledge your complaint within 48 hours and resolve it within one month of receiving it.
provisions.keywords: online app amazon flipkart website grievance officer customer care no reply 48 hours one month e-commerce

provisions.title: Deadline for paying wages
provisions.summary: Monthly wages must be paid before the end of the 7th day of the next month. Weekly wages are due on the last working day of the week, and daily wages at the end of the shift. If you resign or are removed, dismissed or retrenched, or the workplace closes, your dues must be paid within 2 working days.
provisions.caveat: The government can set different time limits in some situations. Check your state's rules.
provisions.keywords: salary wages not paid late delayed tankhwah vetan pagaar 7th full and final settlement resignation fnf

provisions.title: Only allowed deductions from wages
provisions.summary: An employer can deduct from wages only for the reasons the Code allows, such as fines for specified misconduct, unauthorised absence, damage or loss, or advances. Other cuts are not allowed.
provisions.keywords: salary cut deduction kat gaya less salary fine notice period recovery

provisions.title: Wage claim before the labour authority
provisions.summary: Claims for unpaid or short-paid wages are heard by an authority appointed by the government (usually a labour department officer). You, your registered union, or the Inspector-cum-Facilitator can file. The claim must be filed within 3 years, and the authority should try to decide it within 3 months.
provisions.caveat: Where and how to file depends on your state's rules. Contact your district labour office.
provisions.keywords: labour commissioner labour office complaint claim unpaid salary authority inspector three years

provisions.title: Old wage laws repealed from 21 November 2025
provisions.summary: From 21 November 2025, the Code on Wages replaced the Payment of Wages Act 1936, the Minimum Wages Act 1948, the Payment of Bonus Act 1965 and the Equal Remuneration Act 1976. Rights and proceedings that arose under the old Acts are saved.
provisions.caveat: If your unpaid salary is from before 21 November 2025, a lawyer can confirm which law governs it.
provisions.keywords: payment of wages act minimum wages act old law repealed new labour code

provisions.title: Cheque bounce notice and the 15-day window
provisions.summary: If a cheque bounces, the payee must send a written demand notice within 30 days of getting the bank's information. The person who issued the cheque then has 15 days from receiving the notice to pay. If they do not pay, it becomes an offence punishable with up to 2 years in jail, a fine of up to twice the cheque amount, or both.
provisions.caveat: This is a criminal provision. If you received such a notice, paying within 15 days or getting a lawyer quickly is important.
provisions.keywords: cheque bounce dishonour notice 138 15 days payment demand

provisions.title: One month to file a cheque bounce complaint
provisions.summary: A cheque bounce complaint must be filed in court within one month after the 15-day payment window ends.
provisions.caveat: A court can accept a late complaint only for sufficient cause.
provisions.keywords: cheque bounce complaint court one month deadline

provisions.title: Send a written demand before going to a forum
provisions.summary: Before any complaint or case, send the other side a dated written demand (email, WhatsApp, or a legal notice by Speed Post with tracking) that states what happened, the amount owed, and a deadline (usually 15 days). Keep proof of sending. It often settles the matter, and it is evidence later.
provisions.caveat: This is common practice, not a legal rule (except for the Government, see Section 80 CPC, and cheque bounce, see Section 138 NI Act).
provisions.keywords: legal notice demand letter email first step speed post send notice

provisions.title: What proof to collect
provisions.summary: Collect and keep copies of: the agreement or offer letter or bill, payment proofs (bank or UPI statements, receipts), chats and emails, photos or videos (for example, of the flat at move-out), and any reply from the other side. Make a dated timeline.
provisions.keywords: proof evidence documents screenshot receipt upi bank statement photos saboot

provisions.title: How to treat a legal notice you received
provisions.summary: A lawyer's notice is a demand, not a court order. Do not ignore it. Note the deadline, do not admit anything in a hurry, and reply in writing within the time given if you disagree, keeping proof of sending. A court summons is different: it has a date and court name, and you must appear or be represented.
provisions.caveat: If the notice threatens a criminal case, eviction, or arrest, or it is a court summons, speak to a lawyer (free legal aid: 15100).
provisions.keywords: legal notice received reply respond what to do summons court date vakil ka notice
